claims.exact_statement: For a complete passive system coupled to one heat bath at fixed temperature T, with every work port counted and no other exergy input, a process returning the complete state or its full distribution obeys W_on = T Sigma >= 0. Here W_on is net work into the complete system and Sigma is total entropy production. For a noncyclic process, W_out <= F_initial - F_final.
assumptions: First law Delta U=Q+W_on, with Q entering and W_on positive inward.
Single reservoir at T and Clausius relation Delta S=Q/T+Sigma, Sigma>=0.
System includes material, hidden contact/phase/spin coordinates, actuators/controllers, and stores claimed as passive.
All mechanical, electrical, magnetic, chemical, actuator, and other work/exergy inputs are counted.
For stochastic systems, entropy/free energy refer to the complete state distribution.
source_pointers: Delta F=Delta U-T Delta S=W_on-T Sigma; for a full-state cycle Delta F=0.
Standard first/second-law derivation; no novelty or priority claim.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard thermodynamic passivity bound. A single port may deliver positive work if another counted port supplies it; finite output is allowed when available free energy decreases.

costs.formal_result: No computation required once system boundary and balance assumptions are fixed.
costs.physical_test: Measure all mechanical/nonmechanical input ports, thermal flow and temperatures, complete state, and state return.

claims.falsifier: Repeatable W_on<0 for a full-state cyclic device at one bath temperature with all ports and state measured within certified error.
claims.next_gate: Apply the all-port inequality to the specimen and its contact-profile actuator over repeated closed cycles.

claims.exact_statement: Shaat and Park (JMPS 171 (2023) 105163) state in Eq. (31) that reversible isothermal work is a Helmholtz free-energy differential, but claim nonzero closed-cycle work from a non-potential constitutive term in Eqs. (32)-(35). For the same full-state cycle and same work port, these statements imply zero work and cannot both hold.
assumptions: Eq. (31) applies to every leg of the claimed cycle.
The later delta-W and Eq. (31) delta-W are the same work quantity, or omitted ports are added to reconcile them.
source_pointers: Printed pp. 13-15, Sec. 4.1.1 and Eqs. (31)-(35): reversible balance, free-energy closure, non-potential delta-w_cn.
Printed pp. 23-24, Appendix A.1: per-step energy check, endpoint return, and Eq. (A.4) circle-center work accumulation over 40,000 increments.
claims.novelty_boundary: Scoped source audit, not independent replication or a claim about every physical implementation; raw simulation files were unavailable.

costs.audit: Full author PDF including Eqs. (31)-(35), Appendix A.1, and Fig. A.6.
costs.missing_evidence: Abaqus input/output, raw reaction histories, and explicit profile-switching work.

claims.falsifier: Resolve if the work quantities differ, the complete state does not return, or omitted ports/free-energy changes reconcile the cycle.
claims.next_gate: Obtain simulation data or author clarification and recompute work over the complete specimen-plus-actuator boundary.

claims.exact_statement: The positive-work simulation explicitly changes the rigid-circle profile at intermediate states using a slider mechanism that requires an actuator. The paper asserts the slider contributes zero work because stress is unchanged, but Eq. (A.4)'s reported circle-center force/moment versus material displacement/spin accumulator contains no slider force-displacement term. Slider work is an additional port that must be measured; its net value is unverified.
assumptions: Appendix A.1 describes slider profile changes at States 3 and 4.
Eq. (A.4) includes circle-center material ports but no slider generalized coordinate.
Unchanged endpoint stress does not by itself establish zero work over the actuator trajectory.
source_pointers: Printed p. 17: reported +16.6 and -16 kJ/m^3 cycles and zero-work switching assertion.
Printed p. 23, Appendix A.1/Fig. A.6: slider changes profile and requires an actuating mechanism.
Printed p. 24, Eq. (A.4): work accumulation omits slider force-displacement.
claims.novelty_boundary: This identifies an unmetered port, not proof that the slider's net work is nonzero.

costs.raw_replay: Original .inp/.odb, slider position and actuator reaction/work, force histories, contact histories.
costs.physical_measurement: Slider load cell and calibrated position sensor; measure switching, holding, reset, and control work.

claims.falsifier: Measure full slider force-displacement path and certify net zero work, no uncounted reset/control input, and complete state return.
claims.next_gate: Repeat or re-run the profile/deformation cycle while logging slider and all specimen conjugate ports.

claims.exact_statement: Ideal frictionless unilateral contact with gap g(q,s)>=0 and compressive multiplier lambda>=0 is not an energy source. At fixed geometry, an active quasistatic branch has g=0 and g_dot=0, hence ideal contact power lambda*g_dot=0; an open branch has lambda=0. If the gap depends on slider coordinate s, that slider is an additional work port. Hysteretic switching requires accounting for dissipation or hidden-state change.
assumptions: Ideal normal complementarity contact, no adhesion, frictional drive, or hidden active control.
Admissible quasistatic motion respects active contact constraints.
Any profile coordinate s is counted with its conjugate actuator work.
source_pointers: Shaat and Park, printed pp. 6-7 and 23: normal contact and profile-switching mechanism.
claims.novelty_boundary: The identity rules out a free source in ideal contact but does not determine work at an externally moved profile boundary without its conjugate force.

costs.model: Specify gap, multiplier, branch, and slider coordinate.
costs.experiment: Synchronize contact gap/normal force, slider force/displacement, and specimen force/torque.

claims.falsifier: Verified W_on<0 across a full-state closed cycle with ideal contact, one bath, and all geometry ports included.
claims.next_gate: Measure contact transitions and slider work to decide whether switches are conservative, dissipative, or driven.

claims.exact_statement: The theorem does not exclude powered odd-elastic solids, active odd-mass metamaterials, passive odd-viscoelastic fluids, multibath heat engines, or finite one-shot output from metastable/chemical free-energy decrease. These cases have counted resources, a different response regime, or noncyclic full-state evolution.
assumptions: Powered, chemical, and thermal-exergy inputs are included in accounting.
Passive odd-viscoelastic fluid response is not equated with a source-free static-solid cycle.
source_pointers: Chen et al. 2021: piezoelectric metabeam with electronic feed-forward control.
Wu et al. 2023: odd-mass material enabled by powered sensing, actuation, local computation.
Lier et al. 2022: passive odd-viscoelastic fluids; linear viscoelastic chiral solids require activity.
claims.novelty_boundary: Scope controls only; they do not validate the target passive-contact model.

costs.measurement: Power/voltage/current/drive torque meters, heat-flow and temperature measurements, chemical-potential accounting, cycle time, and reset energy.

claims.falsifier: All input ports and source-state depletion should match output and losses for a powered or finite-store example.
claims.next_gate: Use a powered device as a positive control and compare its ledger to the source-free contact-switching claim.

required_files: slider position and actuator reaction histories
raw_data_falsifier.computed_quantity: W_on_total = every specimen boundary force/torque paired with displacement/rotation + slider force paired with slider displacement + all electrical, magnetic, chemical, and other work ports
raw_data_falsifier.decision_rule: For a repeated full-state cycle at one bath, W_on_total>=0; the reversible source-free limit is zero. Positive material-port output with positive slider input is a driven device. Output with certified zero slider work requires another resource/state change or a failed assumption/measurement.

primary_source_audit.target: Shaat and Park, Chiral nonreciprocal elasticity and mechanical activity, JMPS 171 (2023) 105163
primary_source_audit.result: Eq. (31) conflicts with nonzero closed-cycle work if the same full-system port is meant. The practical cycle also uses a profile-slider actuator whose work is omitted from Eq. (A.4) and whose asserted zero work has not been independently measured.
